quest.title: A Gathering of Outlanders
quest.description: As the Windblume Festival approaches, you and Paimon return to Mondstadt, grasped in the throes of festivity, and take on a rather different commission than you are used to...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Go to the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt and take a look

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Good day, you two. It's nice to see you here at this festive time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sooo... Got any jobs for us?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hmm, I'm afraid I'd struggle to find you any commissions in the near future.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: With the arrival of the Windblume Festival, the only task most Mondstadters are busy with is preparing gifts for their loved ones — but it's customary to do this oneself, without assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Think of this period as the off-season for the Mondstadt branch of the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Spring is here, love is in the air, and everyone wants to relax and enjoy themselves. Even the cats at the tavern next door have been getting lovey-dovey with one other recently.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ew... gross.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know that feeling you get when you burst out the doors after a nice nap, hoping to make it to the store before the limited-edition drinks sell out, only to get there just in time to see the last two glasses snatched away right from under your nose by a couple of pesky lovebirds? That's what this feels like.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's... very specific of you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hehe. Perhaps you two could simply take this chance to—

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! Thank goodness I found you. Um, there's something I need your help with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Sucrose?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Go ahead, Sucrose! We don't have anything else to do right now, anyway.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Phew... Okay.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Here's the situation. I've been appointed as the Windblume Festival Special Ambassador by the Knights of Favonius this year.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: My task is to do good deeds for people during this festival of gratitude and love.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nice one! So how did they decide who to appoint, anyway?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: They spun an empty bottle donated by Angel's Share inside a circle with all our names on it. Whoever's name the bottle stopped at got chosen.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This method seems a bit arbitrary.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I think so too. But everyone said that it was to make it fair, so everyone had an equal chance to become the special ambassador.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: The thing is... I'm not great at dealing with people, so I was really daunted by it at first. But I'm still glad that I got this role!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Luckily, I came up with a way to spur myself on, which has helped. Have a look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that a test tube?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Yep. Every time I do a good deed for someone, I get them to breathe into a test tube. That way, I can collect everyone's "Breaths of Joy."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds... fascinating! Are you gonna use them in your research?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Yes. I believe these Breaths of Joy will serve as valuable raw materials for alchemical transmutation. With any luck, I'll be able to produce something truly miraculous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm... Darn, now Paimon's hungry. ...Wait, you're doing this on purpose, aren't you?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Haha. Actually, I meant something even more exciting than that.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I can't say for sure until I have more test results to confirm my hypothesis, though. Alchemists mustn't make claims they can't live up to.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Anyway... I'm still missing one final Breath of Joy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, is that all you need help with? That's easy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just treat Paimon to a Sweet Madame, then you'll get your last Breath of Joy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, come on! Paimon's doing her best to help, okay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... So does it need to be more, like, official or ceremonious or something?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: No, joy isn't measured in those terms at all.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Let me put it this way: Have you ever planted a fruit seed and cared for it while it grows?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: In the same way that those tender, sweet fruits are the product of your time and effort, the amount of joy derived from an experience is positively correlated to the degree of hardship overcome during it.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: For example, in my case, I would say that to experience a statistically significant amount of joy, I'd have to do something like spend six months developing a medicine formula to a point where it was finally consistently effective.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Similarly, in order to collect a significant amount of joy from other people, I have to find ways to do something sufficiently challenging on their behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, Paimon gets it now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Long story short, you want us to help you find people for you to help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That's pretty tough, given that it's the Windblume Festival and all!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh... I figured since you're such experienced travelers, you might have some ideas, but if even you don't know how to approach this...

choices.text: Don't worry. Leave this to me.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Really? You have a plan?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Experience is on my side.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, if {M#he}{F#she}'s in, then Paimon'll help too... with the talking, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But um, if things don't work out, can Paimon still get that Sweet Madame?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, this is a festival of gratitude and love after all. How could you refuse?

response.speaker: Marjorie
response.text: 'Scuse me, Sucrose, could I borrow you for a second? Package for you...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh, sure.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Be right back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, is that who Paimon thinks it is? That's Collei, right? When did she arrive in Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go say hi!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: ...Yes, you're right.

choices.text: Whoa, someone needs help after all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is wrong with you? That's no way to greet a friend we haven't seen in so long!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Uh — no, not help like in the Windblume sense... It's just... Ugh, how do I explain...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Phew. Only the base is burned. We can still use the cooking pot, it just needs a bit of a wash.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good thing Tighnari's nose is so sharp... Has he been in this kind of situation a lot before?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't let it get you down, Sucrose.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know, it's just... I'm sorry to disappoint Cyno. I guess we'll have to do this again another day.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. I'm not sure if you've noticed...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Collei seems a little... depressed. I noticed she was in a low mood when everyone was talking.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Remember that note she received?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I was just thinking. I wanna try solving this riddle and giving Collei the chance to accept the blessing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, yeah! She's someone who needs your help!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Maybe she'll be willing to breathe into my test tube... But anyway, that can wait.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: As much as I'd like to make progress in my research, I'd prefer to see her smile.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! We'll help out too.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: You will? Then tell me, honestly... Do you... think that this prophecy is for real, too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know how I can find out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Huh... right.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be back shortly.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Alright. Let's meet at the alchemy crafting bench in the city. I've got some thinking to do in the meantime.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: We're back.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Ah, what a shame. You just missed a joke about windmills.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Stop. Please. I don't need to hear it a fifth time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That bad, huh? Hmm, now Paimon really wants to hear it for some reason...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Didn't you say you want to see the Dragon of the East at some point? When are you going?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Tomorrow morning.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: And you? What are your plans?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'll go into the mountains to have a stroll and collect a few plants as samples.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Perhaps I could join you? I'll be looking for inspiration for these card back illustrations.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Found you!

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: I knew I was onto something as soon as I saw the fire.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Wow, you have really sharp eyes!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: That's an Outrider for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh... did we break the fire safety rules or something?

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Actually, you didn't. Strictly speaking, you should have reported your plans first, but since two of our very own alchemists are here... I'm happy to look the other way, hehe...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Ah, yes, introductions! I'm Amber, and this is the Reconnaissance Company Captain, Eula, a good friend of mine.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Good evening. You're friends of Collei, yes? A pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Oh, Amber and Eula! The pleasure is ours. I've heard a lot about both of you from Collei.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Oh really? All positive, I hope...?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: You asked that last time too! ...Of course it was positive...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I'd say... we hear the latest news about you every time you write to Collei.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Haha, glad to know we've made a good impression so far! Anyway, we're just here to collect Collei, so don't let us interrupt your chat.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: C'mon, Collei! We're gonna take you to check out a few scenic spots.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Okay, great!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Heh... Still as high-energy as always.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? You know Amber?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Yes, we've met. She's Collei's most important friend, and for that we're also very grateful to her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's Amber for you. Her outgoing personality means she can make friends with just about anybody.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It's getting late, and we still have a lot lined up tomorrow. I suggest we all head back and get some rest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes. We should preserve our energy.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright. I'll start packing up.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone packs up and says their goodbyes in the dark of night...

choices.text: I get that feeling as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei! Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Oh, hey you guys. What are the chances...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were staring into space just now. Something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um... No, don't worry. I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I was just looking at a Mondstadt children's book in the souvenir shop over there.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: While I was flipping through it, a piece of paper fell out. The writing on it was really mysterious... almost like a prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "If you can do these things, you may light the lantern of utmost joy and receive a supreme blessing."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what does "these things" refer to?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "Find a flower that is not of this world. Find a guide who will never get lost. Find one who would never lie. Find a legend that never ends."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So four things in total. Here, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I asked the lady who owns the store about it, but she said that she didn't know anything about any paper slips.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perhaps we can ask a friend about this later...)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hi there. Sorry to butt in, but... what's the name of that storybook you just mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, it was called "The Boar Princess."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm, that is strange... I've read that book, and it sounds like that note you found has no relation to the story at all.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Do you know her?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon do the honors! Collei, this is Sucrose, an alchemist with the Knights of Favonius. And Sucrose, meet Collei. She's a Trainee Forest Ranger from Sumeru's Avidya Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hello...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: H—Hi...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, this is getting awkward fast... They're both so shy!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So, Sucrose, what are your thoughts on this prophecy? Could it be real?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I, um... W—Without having done any research, I couldn't comment definitively...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Um, but if you want my subjective opinion, I don't think that it's a nasty prank or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why not?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The only people who read children's books are those with a childlike wonder and imagination... or children, of course. I'm sure that whoever put this prophecy there would understand that...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Would they really do this just to spread lies and ruin someone's innocence? I can't imagine anyone being so cruel.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: That's a great take. I love it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Who would wanna hurt a child's feelings?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Okay, so... What do you think the "blessing" is, Sucrose?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm... Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: If I had to guess... Maybe a fairy that can make people's wishes come true, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I haven't read many fairy tales, so this is pure speculation... With no other information on hand or prior research to compare against, I'm afraid it might not even be worth considering.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wow...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Her guesswork is really good, though! I wanna pick her brains some more...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (But will she find it annoying if I keep asking her questions...?)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (We've only just met, after all... Aah, what's the best thing to say to someone you're meeting for the first time?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to get the "lantern of utmost joy"?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Well... Yes, I mean... if possible...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Then, what would you wish for, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um. I'd wish for a... a better personality.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can't waste it on that! You've got a great personality already!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: That's very kind of you, but if you know me like I do...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I know that voice! It's...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Collei! Whew...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: You made good time, huh? You're way earlier than I expected!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: I spotted your green hair way off in the distance — good thing my eyes are sharp, or I'd have missed you!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Amber! Have you been doing well? Did you... finish all the Pita Pockets I brought you last time?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: You bet! They're getting yummier each time you make them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, remind Paimon... have you been to Mondstadt before?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: A long time ago, I had a lot of help from a lot of people here in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So ever since my Eleazar got better, I've been looking out for an opportunity to come back to Mondstadt and tell them all the news that I've been cured...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Thanks...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: If it's okay with everyone, why don't I take Collei for a walk around town? I'd like to show her some of the places she didn't get to see last time.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Of course, fine by me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure! Go right ahead!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I, uh...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Umm... sorry Amber...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I agreed to meet my traveling companions by the city gate in a few minutes, so I can't go with you just yet...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Oh, that's alright!

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: In that case, you guys go rest up, and I'll go see Master Jean to ask for some time off.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, okay...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Sucrose, could you look after Collei for now?

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: I'll come get her later and take her out. There's still a whole bunch of people I need to introduce her to!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Sure, no problem.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can count on us.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Awesome. See ya later, then!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Umm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You alright there, Collei? You look kinda disappointed...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I'm just feeling a little shy today... Don't worry about me.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: (Amber wants to introduce me to more of her friends... Am I gonna be able to cope?)

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: (I've only met Sucrose so far, and I'm already struggling to make conversation...)

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: (I wish I had a little more self-confidence. Then I'd find it much easier to make friends with people...)

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah! It's nearly time. Let's go to the gate and see if they've arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Why is this humble windmill such a great view?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I mean, it's understandable. It must have been a long time since you last came to Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because it is the true "Great Vay-iew-vyastra."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, come on. Don't tell me you don't get it?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: View, vayu... and also mahamatra, vayuvyastra... no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari, Cyno, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Phew... Am I glad to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And who's this young lady?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master, this is Sucrose, an alchemist with the Knights of Favonius. We just met.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Sucrose, this is my teacher, Tighnari. He's a highly respected Forest Watcher in Sumeru, and he's also a very famous botanist.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei's exaggerating... I'm Tighnari. Pleased to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, so you have a teacher as well! The pleasure is all mine, Tighnari, Sir.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yup! He's extremely knowledgeable, too!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: And this is General Mahamatra Cyno of the Sumeru Akademiya. He's really famous in Sumeru as well!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Greetings. Though if I might say so, we're purely here for personal reasons. You needn't be unduly concerned with our official positions.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And Collei, there's no need to use my full title. "Cyno" is fine, or "Sir" if you absolutely must.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Indeed. We're not here in an official capacity — just to keep Collei company on her vacation.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Keep me company? But it was you two that insisted on coming...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei is very important to us. We felt obliged to ensure her safety on the long treacherous journey to Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But I've been here on my own loads of times before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about your work though? What if something bad happens while the General Mahamatra's away?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There should be no issues. I have left my duties in the hands of my subordinates and two especially reliable helpers.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh! Sucrose, what were you saying about you having a teacher as well...?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I was just going to mention that — I think we're in a somewhat similar situation. I'm an assistant to Mr. Albedo, Mondstadt's genius alchemist.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, please, Sucrose, "genius" is an unnecessary epithet. It will serve only to leave an exaggerated impression of me in the minds of our guests.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: M—Mr. Albedo... but it is an objective truth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Albedo's here too! Great, the more, the merrier!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone introduces themselves, and exchanges pleasantries.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm. So tell me Sucrose — since your specialty is Bio-Alchemy, what do you know about the antitoxic properties of the Calla Lily?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can we hold off on the nerdy topic for now? Paimon doesn't wanna be left out...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh... As it happens, I've studied the Calla Lily in quite some detail before, with it being a species native to Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I wrote a whole report on my findings... If you're interested, Mr. Tighnari Sir, I can go get it for you!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We're supposed to be here on vacation, and you're already thinking about how to improve your herbal medicines? Also, I thought we'd agreed to take on new identities for this trip?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What new identities?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mine was "Adventurer Cyno, skilled desert explorer," Tighnari's was "technological consultant to the Treasure Hoarders," and Collei's was "traveling musician."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...And you find that sort of role-play fun?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Very much so.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I do wish some of the less cautious adventurers in the Avidya Forest would consider coming to Mondstadt instead.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What Philanemo Mushrooms lack in texture, they make up for in not causing vomiting or diarrhea.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Pfff...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Are you contemplating using some compounds from the Calla Lily as active ingredients in a targeted antidote?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes. I gathered a few on the way here, and my initial research suggests to me that it could be worth a try.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Okay... I got it.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But... as much as I don't wish to be a wet blanket...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It takes a huge amount of experimental data to conclusively prove how different drugs interact. Estimating the total development time would be very difficult...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Add in the time for procurement and delivery of essential materials and I'm not sure if we could complete development before you need to return.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Then please, allow me to help.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Mr. Albedo!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Apologies for my tardy entrance in the present discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I understand you're looking to make an antidote for poisonous fungi, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If you happen to have some samples with you, or relevant documentation on hand, perhaps you might give me the chance to review them later?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But before that, I invite the three of you to look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Food and lodging arrangements!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Were you quietly writing this up the whole time? Paimon didn't even notice!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Impressive multi-tasking.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hardly.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Rather, I should apologize for interrupting a serious discussion between trained professionals, especially after they have traveled so far to be here, when I myself am neither an adventurer, nor a technological consultant, nor a musician.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, I would encourage you to have a knowledgeable local arrange your detailed itinerary while you're in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Take a look, and should you find anything here to be objectionable, it can easily be adjusted.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This is too kind of you. These arrangements are quite excellent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks great! Even Paimon feels like tagging along for the food and board...

choices.text: You're not included in this itinerary...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why it's called "tagging along"!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Very comprehensive. The adventurer, technological consultant, and musician all approve. Thank you.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Just one thing... We'd like the chance to cook as well. Why don't we change the group dinner to a camping and cooking trip?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I'll help pitch the tents!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I can help too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um... and Paimon will take {M#him}{F#her} to Good Hunter to order some starters. Mondstadt's Cold Cut Platter is not to be missed!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Great. Then it's decided.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Sucrose and I will bring the three of you to your inn for a quick rest. You two, let's meet by the lake this evening.

choices.text: Ah, I'm looking forward to it already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, doesn't Paimon's opinion matter anymore? Paimon's technically a guest in Mondstadt too, y'know!

talks.objective: Go to Good Hunter and order some food

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Sara, can we have a Cold Cut Platter to go?

dialogues.speaker: Sara
dialogues.text: Sure, coming right up!

dialogues.speaker: Sara
dialogues.text: Would you like anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, do we, uh, want anything else...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Okay, uh... yeah, that'll be all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know what? Let's have a Sweet Madame as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay! You're the best person in the whole wide world!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon'll give you the Sweet Flower from that Sweet Madame as a Windblume!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just don't ruin your appetite for later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe! No need to worry about that! Paimon can make room for good food!

response.speaker: Sara
response.text: Haha, alright, just a moment...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: In the time it takes Sara to pack up the Cold Cut Platter, Paimon polishes off the entire Sweet Madame...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Mmm... That was great.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If that was a Windblume treat, then Paimon wishes it could be the Windblume Festival every day!

choices.text: Ugh... if we must — one Sweet Madame, I guess.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, so you do remember after all! You're just the best!

talks.objective: Head over to the camping site

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Alright, looks like we're all here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're not late, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Not at all. We just came early to set everything up, since we happened to be free today.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Collei put up the tents so quickly, but still managed to tie very sturdy knots. You can really tell that she's a professional.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I didn't do much apart from passing materials around...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Heh, thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to Master and Cyno. They taught me everything I know...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What can I say. For a skilled adventurer, this is just another day on the job.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ugh... Are you quite finished, or were you going to sing each others praises till the moon rises? Come on, let's all sit down.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That Sunshine Sprat was really very good. I didn't watch you cook it, but I believe that the prominent umami flavor of the dish owes itself to more than the fish alone.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's correct. Any further deductions?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let me think... The aroma was quite uniform, unlike that of a spice blend. It was also unfamiliar to me, so I would venture that it was a Mondstadt specialty.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As far as edible Mondstadt plant species are concerned, Calla Lilies are usually used in soups. So if I had to guess...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Small Lamp Grass?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I've long heard that Sumeru's Fish With Cream Sauce is noted for its gentle texture, which brings out the tenderness of the fish.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Here in Mondstadt, we're not quite as varied in the use of spices as in Sumeru, but the principle of bringing certain distinct flavors to the forefront through combinations of natural ingredients is very much the same.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I liked it a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm curious as to the exact ratio of ingredients...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll write a copy of the recipe for you.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Would anyone like to try the nutrient-dense meal I made?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll have some.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: What about you, Collei? It doesn't look like you've eaten very much. Is your appetite low at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uh, no... I just don't eat a lot normally.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um, sorry, I didn't mean to make things awkward...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tighnari. While we were on the road, we spotted something white, walking on two legs. Was that Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Which day was this?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Just after passing through Stone Gate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Cyno, are you sure your eyes were working that day? Or maybe your hood was blocking your vision?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon always flies. There's no way she'd ever walk.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is that right...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I thought that you'd maybe snacked on too many local... ground nuts.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No? Not funny?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ground, you know, as in "ground up," but also "the ground"... ground nuts make you fall to the ground...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Think of this as part of the process of getting to know Cyno. On the bright side, these jokes show that he thinks of you as his friends.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Still, we could test the hypothesis?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What hypothesis?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: That plant species indigenous to Mondstadt may have an effect on the motor functions of flying lifeforms.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon's not your test subject!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, by your logic, wouldn't that mean that eating... say... Zaytun Peaches — that would make a sick Paimon peachy in no time, or something?

choices.text: Or that eating enough Lavender Melons would... uh... have no effect.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, not you too!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Hahaha...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: #I think {NICKNAME} and Paimon's conversations are more entertaining than Cyno's jokes.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...I see. You must have been keeping quiet about this grievance for quite some time now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You seem much cheerier now that you're here in Mondstadt, Cyno. Actually, it feels like you're a completely different person!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That's because I'm Cyno the Adventurer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's not funny.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Hmm? It's not?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: In fairness, you only saw him in his work mode while you were in Sumeru. He's actually like this most of the time when he's in a good mood.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Yep, it's true. Sometimes when he's eating, he'll grumble about how the bowl is too shallow for the amount of food it contains, and other random stuff like that.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I understand. Then allow me to reintroduce myself. Before, you knew me as General Mahamatra Cyno. Now, please see me as Cyno the Adventurer.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yeah, so that's another thing he does! He'll keep repeating something he thinks is funny until you stop trying to resist.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Hmm, so you have two different mental states? Almost like... different phases of matter? Interesting... I want to learn to do that, too!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I think in your case, the two states we would end up with would be highly conscientious Sucrose and stupefied Sucrose.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Oh, by the way — was there any reason in particular that you chose Mondstadt as your destination on this occasion?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, well, Lisa once told me that the Windblume Festival is one of Mondstadt's biggest events of the year.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I wanted to take this opportunity to give everyone a Windblume, as a token of my heartfelt gratitude for everything they've done to look after me...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Plus, it was a good chance for Collei to get out and meet some new people.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: "Collei Lily."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Collei's Windblume. Maybe she should call it a "Collei Lily." It sounds very Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: There's also "Collei Flower," which would technically make more sense, but somehow it doesn't sound as nice.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...Moving swiftly on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, he just completely ignored the joke and carried on the conversation. Guess sometimes, that's the only way forward.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...Sumeru's been through some major changes recently, and things at work have only just started to calm down.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I don't get many opportunities to take a vacation, and this was a chance to join Collei on her trip while also learning a few things about Mondstadt's flora and fauna that I'll be able to pass on to my peers and students on my return. Two birds with one stone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about you, Cyno?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I came to ensure Collei's safety.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: That's just an excuse, plain and simple.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Also... there's the matter of a Genius Invokation TCG custom-made card back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aha! So you DID have an ulterior motive!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Have you all played Genius Invokation TCG before?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: And that is why I am proud to call you my friend.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: When I first began contemplating getting a new card back, I asked around before eventually deciding to ask the legendary Mr. Calx for guidance.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: A friend of mine, Sawada, whom I play cards with on occasion, had been to Inazuma for the Irodori Festival. He told me that Calx was a Mondstadter, so I should try my luck there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Calx? Uh, isn't that...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You mean, he's a friend of yours?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I see, so you came to Mondstadt in search of Calx.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: No, that is inaccurate. I came here principally to protect Collei.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You most certainly did not. Collei's been here on the quiet numerous times, and this is the first time you felt the need to join.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Not only me. Same applies to you too, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If my writer friend were here now, I'm sure he would describe this curious coincidence as having the makings of a good story. It's always a pleasure to meet a fan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, here it comes!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Wait, you mean, you're Mr. Calx!?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Having my new friends address me by my pen name feels somewhat unusual. Please, just call me Albedo.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Huh. So you're Calx... Cyno's been talking about you non-stop recently. He's intent on getting you to design a bespoke card back for him.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ugh, you didn't have to say all that...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I don't usually take private commissions, but I believe that we are friends now. All of us.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Our conversations have been deep and interesting. And Cyno, your passion for this game is indeed one of a kind. I can see it in your eyes.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Obviously.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: And given that you've come all this way from Sumeru to see me, I'd be quite honored to take this commission.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Wow, your teacher's... so nice.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I feel the same about yours. Hmm, well, they definitely have quite different personalities, but they're similar when it comes to their character.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So. How much should I budget for the timeless masterpiece you will produce for me...?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Surely "timeless masterpiece" is something of an overstatement.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Any artwork fit to appear on the reverse of my card decks is by definition a timeless masterpiece! Even if I do say so myself.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Don't mind him — these TCG nut jobs are all like this...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I see. So this has an almost religious significance... Well, for starters, I'd like to hear a few more of your jokes.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: My jokes? You like them?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I do.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Really? I didn't see you laughing.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Well, a joke's ability to induce laughter is a separate matter. But I certainly find them fun.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If I might interrupt, does anyone else smell something strange?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Ah! My nutritional meal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will it be okay? Should we go over and take a look, too?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Well, you should. For the sake of our continued friendship.

choices.text: I say we put these theories to the test!
Is no one gonna stop him from explaining?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'd be grateful if you could check on Sucrose. As for our new friends here... leave them to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're gonna get the Tone-Deaf Bard to check out that note, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess Paimon knows you pretty well, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Knowing him, he should be hitting the taverns around this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can go corner him and make him answer our questions. Let's move!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Or given the way that you're staring at me, perhaps... you'd like to get me that drink now?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I, of course, would be most amenable to that... but I believe you have friends waiting for you?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Don't worry! There'll be plenty of time during the festival.

talks.objective: Go to Angel's Share and look for Venti

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oho, it's been a while!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon called it! Tone-Deaf Bard, drinking as usual!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Put your drink down and get your game face on. We've got some important questions for you, mister.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Uh... Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Venti about the mysterious prophecy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do you make of it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, any thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, aren't you forgetting something? It's the Windblume Festival right now. You can't just go around asking people for help so blatantly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if you won't tell us the answer, could you at least tell us if this thing's worth a shot?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Sounds to me like you want a hint or two?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And a blessing or two to boot.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, a fine answer.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The person who wrote this prophecy is very powerful. If you manage to solve the riddle, good things are sure to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Also... I happen to know where this lantern is.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Once you've found the four things, I'll even write the location down for you. Isn't that generous of me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, whatever. We weren't expecting much from you anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can get back to guzzling wine and blowing wind now, hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, woe is me... Paimon sees me as nothing more than a drunken wastrel...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: There are actually a great many things that we bards are required to do... It just happens that enjoying life is the most important one.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Once this is over, would you like to join me for a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Y'know... A favor for a favor?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: "A flower that is not of this world." Hmm, not of this world...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sucrose! We've got some good news and some bad news. Which would you like to hear first?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Um... Let's have the bad news first, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, really? Don't most people usually want to hear the good stuff first?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just get to the point, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, alright then... Basically, we went to Windrise to divine the breeze.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The wind said that the prophecy is real, and that your idea is a really good one.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound like bad news... So what's the real bad news, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon ate the bad news, hehe~!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Blame Cyno! If it's not funny, then it's his fault!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hehe... It's fine. Well, that puts my mind at rest.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Now, back to the other issue I've been mulling over.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I was thinking about the flower that is "not of this world." It could mean a human-cultivated variety that doesn't occur in nature... But that's basically claiming that it doesn't come from this world in the first place, when actually it's just a variant of an existing breed.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So the initial question is: Can the flower's origins be traced back to a natural organism? If so, it cannot be correctly described as "not of this world."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But then... supposing we identified something outside of that category, whose job would it be to decide whether it belongs in this world or not? Then the question becomes: Do "of this world" and "from this world" mean the same thing... or is it deeper than that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, slow down... Paimon's head is already starting to spin.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Okay. Um... I did have one other line of thought as well. What about a flower created using alchemy? Would that be "not of this world"?

choices.text: If by that, you mean a flower from beyond this world...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Albedo may know the answer, but asking him right away would be like asking the teacher for the answers to your exam paper.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: It would render our search for the truth meaningless. I'd rather try and figure this out for myself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could it be the "Windblume"?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh... now that you mention it, that's definitely a possibility.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: The Windblume doesn't refer to a specific flower. Everyone defines what it means for themselves.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: In which case, the "Windblume" doesn't exist in reality... Hmm. This does seem like a promising direction!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I've made a note! Okay, I'd better go read up on this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay! Paimon was actually useful this time! Guess we have that Sweet Madame to thank, huh?

choices.text: Even a broken clock is right twice a day.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I'll need some time to prepare. Could we meet up here in, say, two days' time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing. In the meantime, we'll also think about the other three riddles in the prophecy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But uh, since we're really going for this now... Shouldn't we say something to Collei about it?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I originally wanted to leave it as a surprise for her, and I also didn't want to get her hopes up over nothing...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: But you're right, Paimon. I'll need to be careful how I word it... but I'll try to find some time over the next couple days to mention it to her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Alright. Thanks so much!

choices.text: We're counting on you for the rest, Paimon.
Albedo did make something like that once.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: ...And that's everything. Are they all in satisfactory condition?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: ...Yep. Thank you, Marjorie.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm. So, a good joke is not necessarily required to make people laugh at them...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, Albedo and Sucrose were delightful... but this was still an exhausting meal.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The cooking pot... Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone brings out their food and starts cooking...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: \nAfter a delicious feast, everyone sits around the campfire...
